MindOn claims 142 garments per hour in an extended folding demo

A person supplies each garment to the dual-arm robot; the entire laundry workflow is not automated.

Humanoids Daily ↗12 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 1

A measurable extended demonstration

MindOn’s 59-minute, 22-second Mind-1 upload shows a counter reaching 142 and labels the footage normal-speed. The company claims 142 garments per hour, roughly 25 seconds each, adding a throughput figure absent from its earlier demonstration.

People still feed the station

Two robot arms fold at a table rather than on a walking humanoid. A person supplies each new shirt, so the demonstration measures a human-fed folding station, not an unattended washing, drying and storage workflow.

No common fastest-in-industry test

The speed superlative remains a company claim without a common comparison of garment types, starting conditions, fold quality and assistance. Extended footage offers more evidence than a highlight reel but does not establish performance across complete laundry operations.
